title: EKS upgrade orchestrator (fleet-fabric) Terraform module for private control plane
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module and orchestration pattern ("fleet-fabric") to automate rolling upgrades of Redwood Private EKS control planes across customer VPCs. The module should support cross-account execution, preflight health probes, automated canary windows, graceful kube-apiserver drain/evict ordering, and an upgrade-status dashboard. It must be idempotent, auditable (CloudTrail/KMS-friendly), and operable both from our management account and customer-managed operatorless flows.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes a stable interface for: target cluster selector, upgrade strategy (serial/parallel/canary), preflight checks, and rollback policy
Module runs idempotently and completes an upgrade end-to-end in a staging fleet (documented runbook)
Preflight health checks fail-fast for control-plane API latency, kube-controller-manager errors, and nodegroup drift; failures trigger automatic rollback and create an incident in Ops channel
Upgrade events are emitted to CloudWatch/Datadog with tagging to correlate to customer and cluster, and dashboard shows per-cluster progress
Cross-account execution uses assume-role pattern; no customer KMS keys are moved or exposed; security review sign-off completed
implementation_plan: Design V1 API for module (inputs/outputs) and publish RFC to Confluence
Prototype: terraform module that can trigger eksctl/eks APIs via a Lambda runner in management account
Add preflight health probes: api-server latency, etcd raft leader stability, controller-manager crashloops
Implement canary window: allow 1-2 control-planes to upgrade and monitor for X mins before proceeding
Integrate CloudWatch metrics -> Datadog dashboard and create upgrade-status SNS for Ops
Security review and pen-test of assume-role implementation
Roll out to staging fleet, run 3 end-to-end upgrades, capture learnings, then schedule gradual production rollout
